Canada–Panama Free Trade Agreement, in force 1 April 2013

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Republic of Panama, Ley 23 de 27 de abril de 2015 on prevention of money laundering and financing of terrorism, as amended and consolidated by Ley 70 de 25 de octubre de 2019; implementing regulation for the Registro de Beneficiarios Finales issued under Decreto Ejecutivo No. 93 de 2020; Registro Público de Panamá rules on beneficial ownership filings; Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF) circulars on customer due diligence and PEP risk management

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registro Público de Panamá — Dirección de Negocios Jurídicos

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notaría Pública del Circuito de Panamá

General Power of Attorney executed by foreign shareholders and beneficial owners, together with certified identity documents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent Notary Public of the foreign shareholder's jurisdiction of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization depending on the origin state

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, directors, officers, resident agents and ultimate beneficial owners against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and Panama UAF/MEF freezing lists, pursuant to Ley 23 de 2015 as amended; PEP identification under FATF standards requires enhanced due diligence, independent compliance sign-off, and documented source of funds for any politically exposed person; the B2B cross-border marketplace with SWIFT and Alibaba Pay rails is subject to platform-level customer identification and ongoing transaction monitoring commensurate with its Low_Risk_Standard banking classification.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá — Sistema de Reserva de Nombres en Línea (official online name clearance module of the Registro Público de Panamá)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names may be registered in Spanish or in any language transliterated into Latin characters; the legal name must include the distinctive denomination followed by the universal suffix 'S.A.' or the words 'Sociedad Anónima'; any name originally in a non-Latin script must be accompanied by a Spanish transliteration certified before a Panamanian notary, and phonetic or graphic similarity to an existing registered name is grounds for automatic rejection.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant or its legal counsel must file a written administrative appeal (Incidente de Apelación) with the Dirección General de Negocios Jurídicos of the Registro Público de Panamá within five business days; the appeal must attach the official name-search certificate, a comparative table of registered names, and a legal brief demonstrating absence of phonetic or visual confusion; the Registry issues a reasoned resolution within ten business days. If the administrative appeal is denied, the applicant may file an amparo de garantías before the Sala Tercera de la Corte Suprema de Justicia or submit a revised corporate denomination.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A physically locatable registered office is mandatory: the Sociedad Anónima must be domiciled at the office of a licensed Panamanian resident agent (agente residente), and pure mail-forwarding virtual boxes are not registrable. Operational substance, however, may be virtual: board meetings, management decisions, ISIC 4791 platform servers, and B2B marketplace sales processes may occur outside Panama without creating Panamanian-source income under the territorial tax system.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Estimated 15–25% probability of an unannounced on-site verification of the resident-agent premises and UBO documentation file within the first 12 months; probability increases if the B2B platform routes transactions through Panamanian bank accounts rather than foreign PSP wallet rails; random and thematic UAF inspections of resident agents' AML files are standard practice.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Panama Law 32 of 1927 (Ley General de Sociedades Anónimas), as amended; Articles 1 through 64 (formation, corporate purpose, share capital, registration) and Article 65 (board of directors and officers).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá (Public Registry of Panama), Sección de Personas Jurídicas (Mercantile Section)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública de Constitución (Notarized Public Deed of Incorporation)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no escrow account requirement. The capital stock may be expressed in shares with a par value as low as one cent; at least one share must be subscribed and issued.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the subscription of the Corporation's authorized share capital is hereby ratified, and the shares are allotted to the initial shareholder as recorded in the stock ledger. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office of the Corporation at Panama City, Republic of Panama, as stated in the deed of incorporation, is hereby adopted for statutory service and corporate purposes. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the following officers be and hereby are appointed: President, Secretary and Treasurer, each to hold office until the next annual general meeting, with authority to open bank accounts, execute contracts, and take all necessary actions to operate the electronic B2B marketplace platform.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Search and Availability Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Dirección General de Registro, Panama City
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name search request in person or through the Public Registry's online portal for the proposed name 'PA_CORP B2B Marketplace, S.A.' and at least two alternate names. The Registry verifies that the proposed name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered entity. If available, the name is reserved for the incorporators.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name and alternatives
Identity document or passport of the incorporator or authorized representative
Name search application form
Contact information of the applicant
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected due to similarity, the Registry issues a written notice. The applicant may submit up to three alternative names, which are processed within two business days at no additional official search fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of the Public Deed of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notaría Pública de Circuito, Panama City
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare and review the Escritura Pública de Constitución containing the corporation's name, registered office, corporate purpose (electronic B2B wholesale platform), share capital, and governance provisions. Appear before a Panamanian notary with the incorporators and the registered agent. The notary verifies compliance with Law 32 of 1927, witnesses signatures, and issues a notarized copy for inscription.
required_dossiers: Draft articles of incorporation (public deed content)
Valid passport or national identity card of each incorporator
Appointment and written acceptance of the resident agent (registered agent)
Payment of notarial fees and stamp paper (Papel Sellado) as applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies omissions or legal inconsistencies, the incorporators may sign a corrected deed before the same notary without restarting the process. The corrected deed is re-notarized within one business day.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Public Registry Inscription of the Corporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Sección de Personas Jurídicas (Mercantile Section)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarized Escritura Pública de Constitución with the Public Registry for official inscription. The Registry examines the legality, name, corporate purpose, and registered agent appointment. Upon approval, it assigns a corporate folio number (Ficha) and records the corporation in the mercantile registry. Official filing fees must be paid.
required_dossiers: Notarized Escritura Pública de Constitución
Original and copies of the deed
Registered agent acceptance letter
Valid identification of the legal representative if acting for the incorporators
Official fee payment receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a defect notice or Nota de Advertencia, the applicant must cure the defect within the stated cure period (typically 5 to 10 business days) by amending the deed or filing additional evidence. Re-submission is processed within three business days after cure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration and Municipal Operating Notice
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) – Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas; Municipio de Panamá for Aviso de Operación
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the corporate folio is issued, apply for the Panamanian taxpayer identification number (RUC) with the DGI. Concurrently, file the Aviso de Operación with the Panama Municipality to obtain municipal clearance for operating an electronic B2B marketplace. These registrations enable tax filing, invoicing, and municipal compliance.
required_dossiers: Certificate of corporate folio (Ficha) from the Public Registry
Certified copy of the notarized deed of incorporation
Identification of the legal representative
Lease agreement or address proof for the registered office
Aviso de Operación application form
RUC application form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DGI or the municipality queries the application due to incomplete information, the applicant may submit a rectification via the Panama Emprende portal or in person. The authority issues a certificate of inconsistencies within three business days, and the applicant has five business days to comply.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registered Agent Confirmation and Corporate Books Approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá and the designated Resident Agent (Residente de Sociedad Anónima)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm the resident agent's formal acceptance and maintain the registered office address in Panama City. Prepare and open the statutory corporate books, including the share register and minutes book, and obtain the corporate seal. The resident agent must keep evidence of compliance with the mandatory Panamanian registered agent requirement. At this point the corporation is ready to open a bank account and begin commercial operations.
required_dossiers: Registered agent appointment and acceptance letter
Corporate folio inscription certificate
Certified copy of public deed
Board resolution adopting the registered office
Corporate books (stock ledger and minute book) for stamping
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Public Registry rejects the registered agent's acceptance or corporate books, the corporation must appoint a substitute resident agent and file a new acceptance with the Registry within five business days. Defective books may be corrected and restamped by the notary or the Registry as required.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable – Panama does not mandate an industrial license for electronic B2B marketplace operators under ISIC 4791 (retail sale via internet) or NAICS 425120.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No separate industrial operating license is required. Only the general municipal Aviso de Operación and DGI RUC registration are required.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – the online B2B marketplace activity involves no physical construction, industrial plant, or waste-generating process and therefore does not fall under the Environmental Impact Assessment categories of Law 7 of 2018.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable – the platform operation generates no industrial wastewater, air emissions, or hazardous waste. If the company maintains an administrative office, ordinary municipal solid waste collection and compliance with national waste regulations apply.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No industrial fire safety certification or structural load inspection is required for the online marketplace operation. If a physical office or server room is leased, the premises must comply with the fire safety standards of the National Civil Protection System (SINAPROC) for commercial occupancy, and employees must be registered with the Caja de Seguro Social (CSS) and comply with occupational health regulations of the Ministry of Health (MINSA).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Autoridad Nacional de Ingresos Públicos (ANIP), created by Ley 366 de 2023 as the successor to the Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF) and the Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas (ANA). Primary portals: institutional site anip.gob.pa and taxpayer e-filing platform Sede Electrónica (sede.anip.gob.pa, formerly sede.dgi.gob.pa).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate the Sociedad Anonima (S.A.) with a licensed resident agent at the Registro Publico (Public Registry); nominal registered capital suffices and no minimum paid-in capital is required. Step 2: Obtain the Aviso de Operacion (business operation notice) from the competent Alcaldia/Municipio and pay the municipal operating tax (patente). Step 3: Register for the RUC (Registro Unico de Contribuyentes) with ANIP through the Sede Electronica, declaring the ISIC/CIIU activity codes (4791 for e-commerce wholesale platform operations) and obtaining the definitive RUC certificate; non-resident shareholders may act through a notarized power-of-attorney holder. Step 4: Activate the ITBMS (VAT) taxpayer account and, if any local employees are engaged, register with the Caja de Seguro Social (CSS). Step 5: Obtain a digital signature certificate (certificado de firma electronica) and enroll in ANIP's electronic invoicing (facturacion electronica) environment before issuing invoices. Step 6: File monthly ITBMS returns (accounting-taxpayer forms), the annual corporate income tax return (Formulario 200), and, where applicable, the annual informative foreign-income schedule to evidence territorial-source treatment.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Territorial_Scope / Entity_Level_Taxation: The Panama S.A. is an autonomous juridical person taxed at entity level on income from Panama-source activities only; foreign-source income realized through cross-border B2B marketplace operations is outside Panamanian income tax, although a nil annual return remains mandatory. The standard corporate rate is 25% on Panama-source net taxable income; no pass-through or transparent treatment exists for an S.A.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No U.S.-style check-the-box classification and no hybrid-mismatch election are recognized under Panamanian territorial law. Available elections include: (i) the Regimen Especial de Pequenos Contribuyentes (special small-taxpayer regime) available where annual gross income is equal to or below B/.36,000, substituting a fixed quota for full ITBMS administration; (ii) the election between the 10% tax on dividends actually distributed and the 5% deemed-dividend (dividendos presuntos) regime computed on book profits in the annual ISR return; and (iii) consolidated ISR filing for affiliated groups meeting the 90% common-control and ANIP authorization conditions.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS - Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios (Panamanian VAT/GST) supplemented by municipal gross-receipts tax (Impuesto de Operacion / patente)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general de-minimis threshold: any person habitually transferring taxable goods or rendering taxable services within Panama must register for ITBMS upon commencement of taxable activities. A special simplified regime ceiling of B/.36,000 in annual gross income allows election of the fixed-quota small-taxpayer regime. Non-resident digital-service suppliers are required to register through a simplified procedure when their B2B/B2C digital services are consumed or used in Panama.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory phased electronic invoicing under Ley 71 de 2019 and ANIP executive regulations. Registered taxpayers must issue Factura Electronica through ANIP's e-invoicing portal, transmitting invoices to the fiscal platform in real time (online mode) or at least once every 24 hours (offline mode) via the ANIP REST API, with XAdES digital signature certification, ANIP real-time validation, and a quick-response (QR) code. Legacy paper 'impresos fiscales' are abolished for mandated groups; marketplace operators, exporters, and large taxpayers must interface their ERP/POS systems with the ANIP fiscal module.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods sold to non-residents and physically exported from Panama qualify for the 0% ITBMS rate when the definitive exit is evidenced by an approved customs export declaration (Poliza/Declaracion de Exportacion). Services rendered to non-resident users, performed from Panama but economically used abroad, including cross-border B2B marketplace services consumed outside Panama, are zero-rated. The taxpayer must evidence the non-resident status of the counterparty, the actual export or offshore use, and the receipt of payment; supplies used in Panama remain taxed at 7%.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Poliza / Declaracion de Exportacion approved by ANA-ANIP through the SIGA customs system evidencing ISIC classification, quantity, value, and definitive exit date
Factura Comercial / Commercial Invoice expressly stating 'Exportacion sujeta a 0% ITBMS' and identifying the non-resident purchaser
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / CMR transport document evidencing the physical departure of goods from Panamanian territory
Inward remittance certificate (Certificado de abono en cuenta / comprobante de transferencia SWIFT) evidencing collection from the non-resident buyer in US dollars or foreign currency
Executed B2B platform service contract and non-resident status certificate substantiating the offshore beneficial use of marketplace services
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating and offshore-service claims are priority targets of ANIP fiscalizacion (tax audit). If the export is disallowed - for example, absence of customs exit, non-collection of payment, or false non-resident certifications - the ITBMS is clawed back at 7% together with monthly recargos (surcharges), statutory interest at 10% per annum, and a compensatory fine of up to 100% of the omitted tax. Simulated exports, falsified invoices, and false residency certificates trigger criminal tax-fraud liability (delitos contra el sistema tributario) with imprisonment of up to 5 years and fines of up to B/.100,000, as well as disqualification from exporter registers and publication of the sanction. Supporting records must be retained for at least 7 years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) pursuant to Decree Law 2 of 2008; Panama does not maintain a formal central bank. The Banco Nacional de Panamá serves as fiscal agent of the State, while the US Dollar (USD) is legal tender and the Balboa (PAB) circulates only as coins at a 1:1 fixed peg.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Panama is a fully dollarized economy with an absolute and unrestricted legal framework for currency convertibility. There are no exchange controls, no capital account restrictions, and no current account barriers to profit remittance, dividends, interest, royalties, or loan repayments. Convertibility is functionally denominated in USD; the practical constraints are limited to correspondent banking AML/KYC screening and US Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) compliance, not Panamanian exchange regulations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender requirements exist. Panama does not impose any mandatory conversion ratio, repatriation timeline, or central bank registration on export proceeds. Exporters may retain, deploy, and wire foreign currency receipts freely, subject only to standard banking due diligence and suspicious transaction reporting thresholds.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account for B2B marketplace settlement; segregated client funds sub-account for merchant payouts
Operational Account in USD; potential escrow/trust clearing account for state-linked trade flows
Operational Account with multi-currency sweep; trade finance and LC desk for regional B2B disbursements
Operational Account and commercial card settlement account for platform fee collections
Operational Account tailored for e-commerce and payment intermediary risk profiles
Operational Account with global clearing connectivity for high-volume SWIFT transfers

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium-High for locally licensed fintech/EMI arrangements; Low for unlicensed offshore digital EMIs. Panama's Law 5 of 2021 establishes an innovation hub and fintech licensing regime administered by the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP). An offshore EMI without a Panamanian banking, fintech, or money-services license cannot legally custody client funds, open local payment accounts, or clear USD in Panama. A licensed local partner or a bank-operated payment gateway is required to channel marketplace receivables and payouts. Such arrangements are viable but require contractual liability allocation, sub-account segregation, and SBP AML/CFT compliance.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In-person presence is not explicitly mandated by statute, but SBP Rule 3-2013 (as amended) requires enhanced due diligence for non-face-to-face onboarding. In practice, Tier-1 banks generally require at least one authorized director or the appointed resident agent with legal capacity to attend an interview in Panama, or to execute a notarized power-of-attorney enabling a Panama-based signatory or bank officer to complete the KYC interview. Remote video KYC is increasingly accepted for low-risk operational accounts, provided original corporate documents, copies of passports, and beneficial ownership declarations are apostilled (Hague Apostille Convention) and submitted through a registered law firm or corporate services provider.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity caused by bearer shares, nominee shareholders, or private interest foundation (PIF) structure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete registry-certified beneficial ownership declaration (Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales), full trust/PIF deed with the economic settlor and current beneficiary identified, notarized identity documents, and a legal opinion from a Panamanian counsel confirming no bearer shares are outstanding if the S.A. was incorporated before abolishment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of funds for the B2B marketplace initial capital injection and subsequent merchant settlement volume
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited bank reference letters from the investor's home jurisdiction, corporate board resolutions authorizing the capital contribution, signed shareholder loan agreements with documentary evidence of remitting bank account ownership, profit reserve calculations, and six months of bank statements from the founding entity demonstrating admissible commercial history.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border payment flows to perceived high-risk jurisdictions or jurisdictions with weaker AML enforcement
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A written commercial rationale for the vendor country base, existing supplier contracts and purchase orders, performed sanctions screening (UN, OFAC, EU, Panama List) through an independent screening engine, an institutional AML/CFT policy compliant with SBP standards, and a periodic transaction monitoring program with clear thresholds and audit trail.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Lack of physical and economic substance in Panama despite the S.A. being a domestic legal entity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Lease agreement for a local registered office or operational administrative presence, employment contracts for at least two Panama-based officers, local bank mandate authorizations, Panama corporate tax filings (ISR), municipal operation notice, and annual fees payment receipts to the Registro Público and the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá, if applicable.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Exposure to digital asset or crypto-related inbound payments, requiring enhanced scrutiny under SBP fintech rules
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Explicit prohibition or strict limitation on crypto/stablecoin settlement in the platform commercial terms, a payment flow map demonstrating that all fiat settlements originate from licensed banking institutions, a legal opinion on the token classification, AML wallet-screening certificates where applicable, and documentary evidence of rejection of non-compliant virtual asset transfers.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injections into the Panamanian S.A. are routed through SWIFT MT103 wire transfers from the foreign shareholder's or lender's bank to the beneficiary account held at a Panamanian Tier-1 bank. There is no Panamanian central bank notification, registration, or prior approval requirement. The transfer's purpose description should state 'Capital contribution - equity issuance' or 'Shareholder loan disbursion', accompanied by a board resolution, updated shareholder registry, and a source of funds letter. Amounts above USD 10,000 will automatically generate bank transaction reports under Panamanian AML law; amounts above USD 50,000 or unusual patterns may trigger enhanced due diligence but remain fully lawful. For a shareholder loan, the bank will request a signed facility agreement, an interest-rate analysis, and a repayment schedule; to ensure a clean deduction for withholding tax on interest, the lender should consent to Panama tax reporting under applicable double tax agreement if any.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlement and payouts to B2B vendors can execute via several permissible rails: direct SWIFT MT103 wire transfers for equal or non-documentary payments; commercial letters of credit (LC), typically issued by the Panamanian bank through MT700 messages, with MT798/MT799 confirmation and modification traffic; MT202/MT202COV for interbank settlement covering underlying trade obligations; and local USD clearing via Panama's automated clearing house operated by Centro de Procesamiento Interbancario (CPI) for domestic payees, allowing next-day USD settlement. For frequent B2B marketplace payouts, a segregated omnibus settlement account with sub-ledgers per vendor, controlled through host-to-host API or SWIFTNet, is operationally recommended, provided the bank's cash management system supports batch transaction formats and sub-account visibility.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: No local FX hedge is required for USD/PAB because of the 1:1 fixed currency board relationship; USD is legal tender
USD/MXN and USD/BRL outright forwards for regional vendor and customer settlement currencies
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on USD/COP, USD/PEN, USD/ARS and Asian offshore currencies such as CNY and INR to hedge B2B supply-chain exposures without requiring local settlement capacity
Cross-currency swaps (USD vs EUR, GBP, or JPY) for treasury liquidity management and interest-rate alignment
Exchange-traded or OTC USD currency options for purchase-order specific flow hedging, executed only through regulated global banks with Panamanian presence or SEC/EMIR-authorized counterparties

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Franchise Tax Payment (Tasa Única Anual de Sociedad)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance, Panama
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due on or before 15 March each year; first-year payment pro-rated based on incorporation date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment accrues a 10% surcharge plus statutory monthly interest; non-payment for multiple years may lead to suspension of corporate rights and administrative strike-off by the Public Registry.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Final Beneficiary Declaration (Declaración Jurada de Beneficiario Final)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) – Beneficial Ownership Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filing due by 31 March each year, reflecting beneficial ownership information as of 31 December of the prior year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance triggers fines up to USD 10,000 per data omission or inaccurate filing; repeated failure may prevent issuance of certificates of good standing and trigger compliance enforcement actions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Declaración de Renta)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance, Panama
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filing due by 31 March following the close of the calendar tax year (31 December); nil returns are mandatory for inactive entities.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing incurs a 10% surcharge plus moratory interest on any unpaid tax; continued non-filing can lead to presumptive assessment and enforcement measures.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit where gross annual revenue exceeds USD 3,000,000, or where the entity is a publicly-listed company, concessionaire, or otherwise required by law or license. Below the threshold, financial statements need not be independently audited unless required by a third party or regulator.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS/NIIF) as issued by the IASB and adopted by Panamanian accounting regulations; no separate local GAAP applies.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Panama's Law 52 of 2016, every corporation must keep beneficial ownership records and file an annual sworn declaration with the DGI Registry by 31 March. Any share transfer resulting in a natural person directly or indirectly owning or controlling 10% or more, or exercising effective control, must be recorded in the Register of Members and reported to the resident agent and DGI within 30 calendar days of the transaction, ensuring continuous UBO confirmation.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 300 – USD 550 per annum for resident agent services including registered office; additional cost if nominee officers or directors are retained.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000 – USD 8,000 for a standard statutory audit where the compulsory threshold is met; not applicable if the entity qualifies for the voluntary unaudited regime.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Territorial taxation applies: foreign-source income is excluded from the Panamanian ISR (Impuesto sobre la Renta) base under Law 8 of 2010, creating an effective 0% rate for offshore receipts. Small-taxpayer preference: enterprises with annual gross turnover below USD 1,500,000 pay a reduced 15% rate on the first USD 50,000 of net taxable income, with the excess taxed at 25%. Export-platform and free-zone preferential regimes (0%–5% tax) exist under SEM and Zona Libre rules but are not assumed for this ordinary Sociedad Anónima engaged in domestic-sourced B2B marketplace intermediation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 820 – Declaración Anual de Renta (Annual Corporate Income Tax Return), electronically filed via the SITIO DGI e-Tax portal (https://sitio.dgi.gob.pa) with the RUC holder's digital signature or the resident legal representative credential.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due within three (3) months after the close of the fiscal year per Article 714 of the Código Fiscal. For calendar-year taxpayers the deadline is 31 March of the following year. No general extension exists; delayed filing triggers surcharge and interest.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: RUC number, verification digit, fiscal period, business name, economic activity code (ISIC 4791 / NAICS 425120), and legal representative data.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The foreign parent or non-resident shareholder is not identified on the form; the Panamanian company must register its RUC and its resident legal representative (agente residente or fiscal representative) in the SITIO database before filing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total Panama-source gross revenue, including platform commissions, listing fees, transaction service charges, and any B2B marketplace ancillary income generated by the local S.A..
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign-source revenue (e.g., commissions booked through a non-resident affiliate without a Panamanian permanent establishment) may be excluded under territorial taxation, but the taxpayer bears the documentary burden of proving the foreign source.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allowable deductions: direct platform operating costs, payment-processing fees, bandwidth, personnel, marketing, and depreciation, all supported by fiscal receipts (facturas autorizadas) matching the SIAS e-invoicing system.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductions for payments to affiliated non-residents (royalties, technical services, intercompany fees) are restated and scrutinized under arm's-length standards; acceptable only if the PANAMA TP documentation file and corresponding WHT on 12.5% royalty/technical-service payments are settled.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income after deductions and any NOL carryforward utilization (maximum 5 years).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Loss utilization is capped at five years and is allowed only if the statutory loss carryforward election was made in the prior year's return; non-resident entities without a PE compute no local net income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 5 – Impuesto sobre la Renta Determinado
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax applied to Line 4: 25% on net taxable income; reduced 15% rate applies to the first USD 50,000 for small taxpayers under the USD 1.5 million gross revenue threshold.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The 25% rate is final for the local S.A.; no consolidation with the non-resident shareholder's home-country income is permitted in Panama.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Advance monthly payments (Formulario 810 installments), source withholdings, and tax credits applied against the annual tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only advances paid by the Panamanian entity under its own RUC are creditable; payments made by a foreign affiliate are not creditable unless remitted as a contribution and re-registered.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 7 – Saldo a Pagar o Saldo a Favor
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final balance due to the DGI or refundable credit resulting from Line 5 minus Line 6.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any refund claim must be lodged through SITIO and is subject to DGI audit; non-resident shareholders cannot offset this balance with foreign taxes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Annex declaring all intercompany transactions, including payments to the foreign platform parent, overseas tech developers, or group treasury.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Check 'Yes' and attach the Transfer Pricing Annex and report whenever aggregate annual related-party transactions exceed USD 250,000; non-resident affiliates must be disclosed by tax residence country and transaction type.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure of dividends declared during the period and computation of the 10% dividend WHT when the profit is distributed to shareholders.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The local company acts as withholding agent on dividend distributions to non-resident shareholders; the 10% WHT is deposited to the DGI via Form 810 even if the shareholder is abroad.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of Form 820: surcharge of 10% of the tax due if paid in the first month after the deadline, plus monthly interest of 1.5% or fraction thereof until settlement; administrative fines from USD 50 to USD 500 under Article 724 of the Código Fiscal for non-filing; RUC certificate suspension and 'cierre' (closure) proceedings for repeated default; criminal liability for fraudulent non-filing.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 810 – Declaración Mensual del Impuesto sobre la Renta (monthly advance payment and withholding return), also filed via the SITIO DGI e-Tax portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due within the first fifteen (15) calendar days following the month of accrual for taxpayers subject to advance payments or for any withholding event (dividend distributions, royalty/technical-service payments to non-residents, salary IRNR).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Monthly advance ISR base computed from the previous year's tax liability divided into twelve installments; also used to report the advance payment of the 10% dividend tax on non-distributed taxable profits for corporations earning over USD 1.5 million.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The formula remains payable irrespective of the non-resident shareholder's distribution date; failure to prepay the dividend WHT exposes the local company to interest and surcharges.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregate withholding tax on non-resident royalty/technical-service payments (12.5%), dividend payments (10%), and Panama-source payments to foreign beneficiaries.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the foreign beneficiary's TIN and residence certificate on the annex; non-filing of the non-resident withholding is independently penalized.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total amount paid to the DGI treasury account for the month; electronic payment receipt is mandatory.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payment must be made from the Panamanian company's local bank account; payments from the non-resident parent's account will be rejected and treated as non-compliance.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Missed or late Form 810 payments: 10% surcharge plus monthly 1.5% interest; after two consecutive missed installments the RUC is flagged in the DGI risk system; officer travel bans and bank account seizures may be ordered.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Panama maintains a very limited DTA network (in-force treaties include the Republic of Korea and the UAE; several signed treaties are not yet in force and must be verified against the DGI published list). To invoke treaty relief the non-resident shareholder must (i) obtain a Certificado de Residencia Fiscal (TRC) from its home tax authority, certified and apostilled; (ii) submit the TRC together with DGI Form 'Solicitud de Aplicación de Tratado' to the Dirección General de Ingresos through the resident agent; (iii) obtain a DGI resolution approving the reduced withholding rate prior to the dividend payment date; and (iv) instruct the Panamanian payer to deposit only the reduced WHT upon distribution. Absent prior DGI approval, the statutory 10% WHT must be withheld and deposited in full; the excess may not be reclaimed unilaterally by the shareholder.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory WHT on royalties and technical-assistance fees for rights used or services availed of in Panama: 12.5% on gross Panama-source payments; treaty reduction possible only under an in-force DTA (e.g., Korea, UAE). Interest paid to non-residents on loans arranged and booked abroad is generally treated as foreign-source income and is therefore subject to 0% WHT under the territorial rule; however, interest bearing on loans secured by Panamanian assets or evidenced as deployed through a Panamanian PE may be recharacterized as Panama-source and subjected to WHT with interest and penalties.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: USD/PAB 250,000 in aggregate annual related-party transactions triggers the mandatory Transfer Pricing Information Annex (Anexo de Operaciones con Partes Relacionadas) and the Transfer Pricing Report to be attached to Form 820; full Master File/Local File documentation under Executive Decree 194 of 2011 and DGI Resolution guidance is mandated for taxpayers with annual gross revenue above USD 4,000,000 concurrently engaged in related-party transactions above USD 250,000; the documentation must be contemporaneous and submitted upon DGI request.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama does not apply the OECD-style Economic Substance Regulations to ordinary local-activity Sociedades Anónimas, but formal ESR-type substance obligations exist for entities enjoying preferential regimes (free-zone operations, SEM multinational headquarters, ship/satellite registries). For this B2B marketplace S.A., the DGI and the AML authorities nonetheless apply a de facto substance doctrine: the company must demonstrate real personnel, physical premises, accounting records, and actual decision-making in Panama; a shell structure with nominee officers and foreign-only management will be recharacterized as an offshore conduit, subject to denial of territorial-source benefits, reattribution of income to the non-resident principal, and anti-immunity measures under FATF grey-list supervision.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate omission of Panama-source platform commissions, inflation of intercompany deductions, use of false invoices (facturas falsas), or failure to file Form 820 despite generating taxable income from the B2B marketplace operations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil surcharge of 10% of the unpaid tax plus monthly interest of 1.5%; administrative fines between USD 50 and USD 500 for non-filing; fraud penalty of 50% to 100% of the evaded tax; criminal prosecution under Law 8 of 2010 and the Código Fiscal exposing the entity to fines of up to twice the evaded amount and imprisonment of the responsible officers of 2 to 5 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Corporate veil piercing applies where directors, managers, or the resident legal representative knowingly sign false returns; directors are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid tax, civil restitution of evaded amounts with interest, travel bans (impedimento de salida), asset embargoes, and criminal imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company or Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating as a letterbox S.A.: no office or staff in Panama, nominee directors with no control, absence of accounting books and source documentation, while the B2B platform receives payments routed through Panamanian bank accounts or SWIFT/Alibaba Pay rails.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Judicial dissolution of the corporation; cancellation of the commercial registration (Ficha) and the RUC; administrative fines under corporate and AML law ranging from USD 1,000 to USD 100,000; disqualification from obtaining banking and payment-processor onboarding; mandatory inclusion in the risk files of the DGI and the UAF.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Nominee directors cannot shield themselves behind the corporate form; those who facilitated the shell for tax evasion or money laundering face civil restitution, travel bans, disqualification from acting as directors for up to 10 years, and imprisonment for participation in a criminal enterprise.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML/CFT Failure and Beneficial Ownership Non-Disclosure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to register the ultimate beneficial owners in the Panama beneficial ownership registry (Registro de Beneficiario Final under Law 254 of 2021 and its implementing decrees); refusal to cooperate with the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF); absence of KYC/CDD controls for B2B marketplace merchants; processing of suspicious proceeds via Alibaba Pay or SWIFT wire without suspicious transaction reporting.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Monetary penalties under Law 23 of 2015 of up to PAB 5,000,000 for legal entities; suspension or revocation of the license to operate payment processing; RUC cancellation; aggravated exposure due to Panama's FATF grey-list status including debanking by correspondent banks; money laundering conviction carries imprisonment of 5 to 12 years and asset forfeiture.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, compliance officers, and the resident agent who concealed the true beneficiary or executed suspicious transactions are individually liable: civil restitution of laundered funds, freezing orders, travel bans, prohibition on leaving Panama, and criminal imprisonment without the possibility of corporate indemnification.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file the Transfer Pricing Annex and Report when aggregate related-party transactions exceed USD 250,000; sham pricing with the non-resident platform parent or affiliated technology providers; transfer of profits abroad without an arm's-length analysis; backdated or missing contemporaneous documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DGI recharacterization of the transactions and upward adjustment of taxable income, with unpaid tax assessed at 25% plus monthly interest of 1.5%; specific fines for non-filing or incomplete TP documentation of up to PAB 50,000; non-deductibility of the intercompany payments; inclusion in the DGI high-risk audit program.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who signed the annual return and attached the false TP annex are personally liable for the additional tax, surcharges, and interest; flagrant mis-invoicing may be prosecuted as aggravated tax fraud leading to civil restitution, travel bans, and imprisonment of 2 to 5 years; group treasury officers abroad may be co-indicted through international cooperation.
